newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-LAST WICKET STAND FRUSTRATES ZIMBABWE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LAST WICKET STAND FRUSTRATES ZIMBABWE.

text.p: A defiant last wicket
partnership of 68 denied Zimbabwe victory in their tour-opening
three-day match against a Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) XI on
Monday.
Set 275 to win, the local side looked on the verge of defeat
at 170 for nine before the last-wicket pair of Mohammad Hussain
and Mohammad Zahid went on the attack to foil the visitors.
Hussain lashed an unbeaten 58 from 74 balls, slamming eight
fours and two sixes while his partner's 28 included three fours
and a six from 42 balls.
Left-hander Hussain, who had earlier claimed four for 68
with his spin bowling, looked to have staked a strong claim for
inclusion in the Pakistan side for the opening test against
Zimbabwe which starts at Sheikhupura on Thursday.
The earlier PCB batsmen had succumbed to the guiles of
off-spinner Andrew Whittal and slow left-armer Grant Flower who
claimed five for 97 and three for 88 respectively on a dusty
wicket.
The tourists, resuming at 107 for two, added 96 in the
opening session before declaring their second innings at 203 for
eight shortly before lunch.
Grant Flower, unbeaten overnight with 59, went on to to make
75 with seven fours and a six while Craig Wishart carried his
score from 16 to 68 not out, hitting six fours and two sixes as
they added 74 for the third wicket.
